title: Tensor extension of a coherent local morphism
statement: Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme [pqf-def-locnoeth], $I$ a quasi-coherent ideal sheaf [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf], $H$ a coherent module and $F$ a quasi-coherent module [pqf-def-coherent], [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let $U$ be an open with $V(I)=X\setminus U$, and let $\varphi:H|_U\to F|_U$. For some $n\geq0$ there is $\beta:I^n\otimes H\to F$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] such that $\beta|_U=\varphi\circ(\mu_n)|_U$, where $\mu_n:I^n\otimes H\to H$ is multiplication and $I^n$ is the ideal-sheaf-data power, including the unit ideal at zero [lem-weil-pbc-ideal-module-product-stalk]. Thus multiplication on $U$ is followed by $\varphi$. No descent through the multiplication image is asserted.

proof.text: Reuse the proved finite-presentation-from-coherence helper in CoherentStalkMapExtends (finite local generators and finite relations, followed by locality). The finite-presentation Hom theorem makes E=Hom(H,F) quasi-coherent.

Conjugate phi by overFunctorEquiv and take its preimage under overEquiv. Its underlying slice morphism is a section s of E on U. Apply the ideal-power section-extension theorem to obtain n and alpha with local scalar values.

The tensor-Hom linear equivalence supplies beta=e(alpha) and its pure tensor evaluation formula. The scalar restriction lemma computes the restriction. The map-preimage equation and inverse identities of overFunctorEquiv cancel the transports and recover exactly phi.

theorem coherent_open_map_tensor_extension
    {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsNoetherian X]
    (I : X.IdealSheafData) (H F : X.Modules)
    (hH : RingedSpace.IsCoherent X.toRingedSpace H) [F.IsQuasicoherent]
    (U : X.Opens) (hI : (I.support : Set X) = (U : Set X)ᶜ)
    (φ : (restrictFunctor U.ι).obj H ⟶ (restrictFunctor U.ι).obj F) :
    letI : MonoidalCategory X.Modules := SheafOfModules.monoidalCategory X.sheaf
    ∃ (n : ℕ) (β : (I ^ n).toModules ⊗ H ⟶ F),
      (restrictFunctor U.ι).map β =
        (restrictFunctor U.ι).map ((I ^ n).toModulesι ▷ H ≫ (λ_ H).hom) ≫ φ
